author: Shay Ben Shabtay
abstract: This paper replicates and extends selected findings from Duflo et al. (2012). I ask whether the effect of camera monitoring and attendance-linked pay on recorded departure differs according to children’s baseline written-versus-oral test status. Using the original replication data, I reproduce the effects on school opening and three recorded-departure outcomes. I then estimate treatment effects for baseline writers and nonwriters. The effect on recorded departure is 26.1 percentage points for writers and 5.0 points for nonwriters. The 21.1-point difference remains statistically significant after adjustment across the three departure outcomes. The residual-departure interaction is positive, while the government-school-marker interaction is imprecise. However, recorded departure depends on checks when schools were open, which treatment itself affected. These exploratory results show different effects on recorded departure across baseline groups; they do not establish whether children left education or transferred.
ai_statement: During May–October 2026, I used OpenAI Codex (GPT-5.6 Sol and Luna, GPT-6 Astra and Luna, and GPT-6.1 Sol) and Claude Code (Claude Opus 4.8, Opus 5, Fable 5, Fable 5.1, and Opus 5.5) to find information, help with coding and data analysis, and provide examples of structure and wording to guide my own writing. I used the tools for copyediting and formatting, and to help prepare the tables, figures, and appendices and check their content, relevance, and presentation against the seminar requirements. Records from multiple conversations with these tools have been preserved to document this use.
appendix_d: The source is Version 1 of replication package E112523V1 (Duflo et al., 2019). The original benchmark programs are Table1_Fig1_update.do, Table-2.do, and Table7_Table10.do in data/Incentives_FINAL/Programs. I reconstruct the selected results in Python and compare them with the published tables and distributed outputs. The supplied Stata programs are benchmarks; I did not execute them in Stata.

The raw departure reconstruction is in scripts/audit_transition_extension.py. The interaction model, clustered intervals, geographic controls, calendar endpoint check, and wild bootstrap are in scripts/audit_transition_scope.py. scripts/audit_sentinel_measurement.py generates the attendance-code flags and algebraic bounds; scripts/audit_transition_sentinels.py generates the exclusion sensitivity. The main bootstrap uses 9,999 school-level Rademacher draws and seed 20260922.

The numerical verification on October 15, 2026 used Python 3.13.4, NumPy 1.26.4, pandas 2.3.0, SciPy 1.15.3, and Matplotlib 3.10.3. It recalculated the attendance coefficient and clustered covariance from the original records, reconstructed Table 10 from raw data, checked the consensus-writing sample and interaction, and verified the saved 9,999-draw bootstrap p-values. All 12 checks passed. This verification does not claim a rerun of every original table, the structural model, or every alternative learning analysis.

The accompanying replication package includes the source data and benchmark programs, reconstruction scripts, saved statistical outputs, an exhibit generator, a README with reproduction commands, and a file-hash manifest. The main table values and coefficient plot are generated from the reconstructed results. Appendix C records the earlier candidate analyses; their stored outputs and scripts are included separately from the main departure analysis.
